Concentric circles are one of those patterns that look harmless until they’re repeated enough times to start doing weird things to your eyes. This piece is all colored sand: pink, purple, blue, green, yellow, orange, red stacked ring after ring around a tiny dark center. The shape stays perfectly circular, but the illusion doesn’t. Depending on where you focus, it reads like a tunnel, a spinning disc, a hypnotic target, or a hole opening up in the middle. I think what makes this one work is how little it needs. Artist Casey Curran creates kinetic sculptures that combine mechanical systems with forms inspired by plants and natural structures. In this prototype, layers of delicate petals are connected so that a single mechanical action produces a rippling movement across the entire structure. Instead of every element moving independently, the motion travels through the sculpture like a wave. This type of movement is central to Curran’s practice. Using motors, wires, cranks and carefully engineered mechanisms, he creates artificial flowers and organisms that bloom, flutter and contract.  The machinery is artificial, but the movement feels strangely organic ,engineering becomes a way of imitating the rhythms of living systems. #art #artist #fashion #avantgarde #design

Rachel Youn creates kinetic sculptures using artificial plants, electric massagers, metal structures, and everyday mechanical parts. Her sculptures question the line between nature, technology, decoration, and artificial life.#flower #plant #nature #art #artist
